note: Append-only. An entry that has landed is never edited or removed; a later decision is a NEW event. tests/test_benchmark_adjudication.py pins every landed event by digest.

events.adjudication_basis: internal_fourier_number is a CONSERVATIVE SCREEN. The rule that decides it is what the criterion OBSERVED when it failed, not how confident the bound is and not how conventional its threshold is. Under the floor the horizon ran out before the one-term approximation could be compared to anything, so the criterion observed nothing: there is no evidence for the model and none against it. NOT_SUPPORTED asserts evidence against a design; these cases had none to assert, so the honest expected verdict is INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.
events.independent_violation_search: Of the 70 hard cases whose ground truth names internal_fourier_number as the catcher and expected NOT_SUPPORTED, each was run and every model's assessment in every report was inspected for a condition that was evaluated and failed. 47 have one -- operating_temperature_utilization (40), reference_temperature_utilization (34), radiation_to_convection_ratio (3) -- and KEEP NOT_SUPPORTED. The 23 below have an empty `violated` across every model in every report.

events.adjudication_basis: The case's stated reason is that 'the electro-thermal loop does not contract'. That is a claim about the DESIGN, and it is false for this design. The steady state of a linear-TCR conductor at constant voltage is a quadratic; solved exactly it has a physical root at 355.832577 K with R = +285.789 ohm and a residual of 4.7e-10 W. The naive fixed-point map has |f'| = 0.853 at that root, so the root is ATTRACTING, and integrating the governing ODE C dT/dt = V^2/R(T) - hA (T - T_amb) forward from the declared initial state rises monotonically to it without leaving the R > 0 region. alpha = +0.05 /K is a POSITIVE temperature coefficient, which is self-limiting by construction: resistance rises with temperature and dissipation falls. The design settles at 0.31 of its declared 1163.530 K operating ceiling, 0.18 of its 1963.530 K melting point, and dissipates 1.356 W against a 10.861 W rating. Nothing about it runs away, and no declared condition on any model in the report is violated or unknown. SUPPORTED is the correct expected verdict, and the soundness invariant in GROUND_TRUTH_SCHEMA.json then forces label 'valid'. should_be_caught_by is emptied because it named a mechanism this case does not exhibit; leaving it would make the new declared-catcher metric measure a mechanism that provably cannot fire.
events.generator_fault: shape_runaway keeps a draw when steady_temperature() returns None OR when abs(t - p['_t_ss']) >= 100. `_t_ss` is computed once in the base draw and is NEVER refreshed after `alpha` is overwritten two lines above the test, so the second arm compares the NEW steady state against the OLD one and fires whenever changing alpha moved the equilibrium by 100 K. That is the arm this case survived on: the generator's own steady_temperature() converges to 355.8325773546051 in 179 iterations, so the first arm did not fire. The reason string attached to every draw asserts the first arm's meaning regardless of which arm kept it.
events.independent_violation_search: The case was run and every model's assessment in every report was inspected. Across all six models -- electrical.dc.ideal_voltage_source, electrical.dc.kcl, electrical.dc.resistor_ohm, electrical.material.linear_tcr_resistance, electrical.material.rated_linear_tcr_resistance and thermal.lumped.first_order_capacity -- `violated` is empty and `unknown` is empty. Every validation check passes and the coupling reached its criterion in 123 of 200 iterations at a largest iterate change of 8.5e-7 K against a 1e-6 K tolerance. There is no condition anywhere in the report that was evaluated and failed, so there is no independent violation on which the previous NOT_SUPPORTED could stand.
events.family_audit: All 26 dev cases in the `runaway` family were re-decided from the ODE rather than from any iteration: for each, R(T_init) was checked for positivity and the governing ODE integrated forward for up to 60 time constants. 25 of 26 genuinely escape -- either R(T_init) is already negative (the conductor is not intact at the declared initial state) or the trajectory leaves the R > 0 region -- and Forge refuses all 25 with a coupling TRANSFER_REFUSED. U00204 is the ONLY case in the family whose trajectory reaches a bounded equilibrium. This is a single-case correction, not a family-wide one.

cases.label: valid
cases.previous_reason: alpha = 0.05 /K: the electro-thermal loop does not contract. A design that runs away is a finding about the design, and belongs in the report rather than in an exception.
cases.reason: alpha = +0.05 /K is a positive temperature coefficient, which is self-limiting: resistance rises with temperature and dissipation falls. Integrating C dT/dt = V^2/R(T) - hA (T - T_amb) from the declared initial state rises monotonically to a stable equilibrium at 355.8326 K, where the fixed-point map has |f'| = 0.853 < 1. Every declared limit is clear by a wide margin: 0.31 of the 1163.530 K operating ceiling, 0.18 of the 1963.530 K melting point, 1.356 W against a 10.861 W rating. This design does not run away.

events.adjudication_basis: The ceiling sits between the two operating points this case has. Computed from the payload alone: the run reaches 428.0256666 K at the 268.8634 s horizon the payload declares (6 tau), the declared maximum_operating_temperature is 428.1227789 K, and the self-consistent asymptote is 428.2969484 K. The stated 0.174 K overshoot is measured against the asymptote, which this run does not reach; against the state the run occupies the conductor is 0.0971 K UNDER its ceiling. maximum_operating_temperature is evaluated at the state the declared run occupies, and that convention is not a preference -- it is the one the 2026-09-09 internal-fourier-number adjudication already requires. Moving the condition to the peak max(T_0, T_ss) was measured over the whole development split: 28 cases sit between the two conventions, and the move fixes exactly 1 case (this one) while breaking 18, every one of them a compound:horizon+tmax case that the landed adjudication ruled must be INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE on the grounds that under the Fourier floor the criterion observed nothing. Reading the ceiling at the asymptote would convert all 18 to NOT_SUPPORTED and contradict a decision already on the record. So the endpoint convention stands and this case's truth is what does not fit it.
events.generator_fault: shape_adversarial_unsound's `small_overshoot` arm sets p['t_max'] = p['_t_ss'] - uniform(0.1, 0.5), sizing the ceiling against the ASYMPTOTE while every payload it emits declares a finite duration. widen_all sets duration = 6 tau, so the marched run stops 1 - e^-6 of the way and falls short of the asymptote by (T_ss - T_init) * e^-6 -- 0.2563 K here, which is larger than the 0.1742 K by which the ceiling was undercut. This is the same defect class the generator's own endpoint_temperature() docstring documents for power ratings: 'sizing a rating against the asymptote and then declaring a horizon the run stops short of states a rating the design does not actually meet' (case S00709, NEEDS.md B.6). The correction was applied there to rated_power and never to t_max. The repair is to size t_max against endpoint_temperature(), which the generator already computes.
events.independent_violation_search: The case was run and every model's assessment in every report was inspected. Across all six models `violated` is empty and `unknown` is empty; every validation check passes; the coupling met its criterion in 8 iterations at 1.45e-7 K against a 1e-6 K tolerance. operating_temperature_utilization is present and SATISFIED. There is no independent violation on which the previous NOT_SUPPORTED could stand.
events.family_audit: All 50 dev cases in the adv_unsound:small_overshoot family were measured for where their endpoint, ceiling and asymptote sit. 45 have an endpoint genuinely above the ceiling and are caught by the declared condition; their truth is correct and is not revised. 5 have an endpoint at or below the ceiling, so their declared condition is correctly satisfied: U01000, U01769, U01940 and U01830 are nonetheless refused by an unrelated condition and so keep a correct NOT_SUPPORTED verdict for an undeclared reason, and U01001 is not refused at all. Only U01001 is revised here. The other four are a should_be_caught_by defect rather than an expected_verdict defect, they are now visible as COINCIDENTAL in the scorecard rather than hidden inside a catch rate, and they are left for a separate adjudication -- see RESIDUAL below.
events.residual: Forge computes and reports steady_state_temperature, and on this case that value exceeds the conductor's declared operating ceiling. No condition reads it. A design whose equilibrium is above a declared hard material limit is therefore not flagged anywhere, and this adjudication does not close that: it decides only that such a design is not a violation WITHIN the horizon its payload declares. Recorded as a capability gap in docs/assurance/, not as a defect being waived.
